title: HD 93683: Tycho, ASAS-3 and TESS eclipse depths from 1990 to 2026 fit one inclination drift of -0.33 deg/yr with central eclipse near 1999; added light from the Be star does not cause the eclipse loss
abstract: HD 93683 (V736 Car) is an O9V+B0V eclipsing binary (P = 17.80 d, e = 0.27) with a Be-type third star. Its eclipses faded in TESS from 2019 to 2026. A prior campaign study and Martin-Ravelo et al. (2024) reported this; the second study proposed dilution by the Be star or a change of the orbital plane. We added Tycho epoch photometry (1990-1993), ASAS-3 (2001-2009), Harvard DASCH plates (1889-1989) and TESS full-frame images, and fitted one model of two limb-darkened spheres on an eccentric orbit with third light and a linear inclination drift to all data. Dilution does not explain the loss: the TESS primary depth fell by a factor of more than 10, but the TESS flux changed by less than 3.1 percent, ASAS-3 V by less than 0.02 mag, and the eclipse width and the secondary/primary depth ratio changed. A fit to TESS alone predicts the ASAS-3 depths of 2002-2008 (0.24-0.26, 0.20-0.21, 0.16-0.17 mag predicted; 0.28 +- 0.04, 0.24 +- 0.03, 0.19 +- 0.02 observed). A fit to TESS and ASAS-3 predicts the Tycho eclipses: Tycho shows dimming at a time shift of -0.28 d (Delta chi2 = 33.4; largest control 2.0) with a depth of 0.2-0.3 mag, and rejects models with third light below 0.3. The joint fit gives di/dt = -0.325 (+0.008/-0.009) deg/yr, i = 90 deg in 1998.7 (+1.2/-0.7), third light 0.51 +- 0.03 and radii consistent with O9V+B0V; eclipses deeper than 0.01 mag lasted from about 1972 to 2022.5. Sensitivity tests (band-dependent third light, free Tycho time offset) give -0.330 to -0.337 deg/yr and 1999-2001. REBOUND integrations show that this rate needs an outer period below about 4 yr (circular outer orbit, third star 8-25 Msun) and below about 12 yr in all tested cases; this agrees with the Gaia DR3 excess noise of 0.81 mas. A blind DASCH search finds no eclipses in 1889-1990 but is sensitive only to long-lasting central eclipses in 1889-1925 (85 percent recovery), so it does not constrain the precession period. Limits: a linear apsidal motion does not fit the Tycho eclipse times (offset -0.29 +- 0.04 d), omega-dot is not determined, the star model is simple, and the MCMC is short.

display.caption: Eclipse depth of HD 93683 from 1955 to 2030. Points: Tycho (1991, diamonds), ASAS-3 (2002-2008, squares) and TESS (2019-2026, circles); filled = primary, open = secondary; depths are scale factors of the joint model times the model depth. Lines and bands: joint linear-inclination model (V band; median and 95 percent of 40 posterior samples). TESS depths are in the TESS band and the model curves are in V. Grey: no DASCH plates.

Dilution test. Left: the flux increase that dilution needs (ratio of primary depths, triangles) and the measured TESS flux (circles, squares); the measured flux is constant to 3 percent. Right: Gaussian width against depth of each TESS eclipse; the width decreases with the depth, which dilution cannot do.

Left: improvement of the Tycho chi2 when the eclipse model predicted from TESS and ASAS-3 alone is shifted in time (free depth scale); the peak at -0.28 d is the detection; side peaks are aliases where one model eclipse falls on the other data eclipse. Middle and right: Tycho (1990-1993) and ASAS-3 (2001-2009) magnitudes near the model eclipses (primary at 0, secondary shifted by +3 d) with the joint model.

citations.reason: We extend this study of HD 93683. We reuse its ASAS-3 point table and its TESS 2-min detection. Our results support a geometric cause, but its linear impact-parameter model put central eclipse near 1980; Tycho data put it near 1999.
Martin-Ravelo et al. (2024, YMDB catalogue) reported the TESS eclipse decrease of HD 93683 and proposed dilution by the Be star or a change of the orbital plane. Our flux data reject dilution.
